tytul: Pickled horseradish sauce for the refrigerator (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the tested NCHFP pickled horseradish sauce: it is kept in the refrigerator and is not canned.

akapity: 2 cups (3/4 lb) freshly grated horseradish, 1 cup white vinegar (5%), 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon ascorbic acid.
Vinegar with less than 5% acidity should never be used in home food preservation.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, horseradish and the other ingredients.
The pungency of fresh horseradish fades within 1–2 months even in the refrigerator, so make only small quantities at a time.
Wash the horseradish roots thoroughly and peel off the brown outer skin.
Grate the peeled roots in a food processor, or cut them into small cubes and put them through a food grinder.
Combine the ingredients and fill them into sterile jars, leaving 1/4 inch of headspace.
Seal the jars tightly and store them in the refrigerator.
According to NDSU Extension, the sauce keeps in the refrigerator for up to 3 months; it cannot be canned.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door, because US refrigerator-pickle recipes assume 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder, while the door can be about 10 °C.
